entries.title: Crowd Rumor Propagation in a Town Square
entries.description: A flat plaza with dozens of colored spheres (people) that randomly walk, collide, and transfer a “rumor” state that changes their color and spawns fading translucent message particles that leave short trails as the rumor spreads across the crowd.

entries.title: Office Building Gossip Flow Between Floors
entries.description: A transparent multi-story building made of boxes with small spheres (employees) moving along corridors and elevators, where a rumor starts on one floor and spreads via brief contacts, visualized as bright links that pulse between people and a side meter showing overall spread.

entries.title: Social Network Rumor Web
entries.description: Floating nodes (small glowing spheres) arranged in 3D space with thin connecting cylinders (friendships); when one node is “infected” with a rumor it flashes and sends traveling pulses along links that can activate neighbors, with node color indicating belief strength and labels for highly connected hubs.

entries.title: Rumor as a Contagion in a Moving Train
entries.description: A long transparent box (train car) sliding along a track with passengers (spheres) inside moving slightly as the train sways; a rumor originates at one end and transfers on close proximity, changing passenger colors and emitting faint mist particles that drift briefly before vanishing.

entries.title: Microscopic Rumor Spread Inside a Brain-Like Network
entries.description: A branching neural structure of semi-transparent tubes where “rumor packets” are small glowing particles injected at one point, traveling, splitting, and merging along paths, lighting up segments as they go and fading slowly to show which regions are most activated.

entries.title: Rumor Flood Through a Medieval City Map
entries.description: A top-down 3D city grid with narrow streets and houses as low blocks, where rumor carriers (colored dots) wander, meet, and pass on rumors; rooftops gradually change color based on the percentage of carriers in each block, creating a spreading heat-map effect.

entries.title: Rumor as a Virus in a Cellular Colony
entries.description: A cluster of semi-transparent cells (spheres) floating in fluid; when one cell hears a “rumor,” its membrane color shifts and it emits tiny particles that can attach to nearby cells, causing them to change color and possibly repel or attract others, visualizing rumor mutation and resistance.

entries.title: Rumor Eruption in a School Playground
